headline: Japanese physicists have shown a way to measure W-state quantum entanglement of three photons in one step, a task first proposed over 25 years ago.
score_reason: Paper dates from September 2025, so this is old research being re-covered; small three-photon experiment.
importance_line: Researchers building photonic quantum computers and communication links get a faster way to check entangled states, though it works only for three photons so far.
summary: ScienceAlert reports that physicists at Kyoto University and Hiroshima University measured the W state, a type of three-particle entanglement, in a single step using a custom optical circuit. They identified it correctly about 87 percent of the time, above the two-thirds threshold needed to show the measurement works. The result, from a Science Advances paper of September 2025, is older research that the outlet re-covers now.
